source.title: CL2R: Compatible Lifelong Learning Representations
source.authors: Niccoló Biondi; F. Pernici; Matteo Bruni; Daniele Mugnai; A. Bimbo

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some tables are duplicated or flattened in the text extraction, but the cited results below are legible.
record.tranche_reason: It measures whether representations from sequentially updated models can be used together for visual search, using cross-test retrieval/verification and compatibility metrics. This is a conceptual test of representation interchangeability, not a test of convergence across independently trained models as they scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports experiments on direct cross-model feature compatibility. Its discussion of other studies is not recorded as results. The paper also reports classification/forgetting results that do not themselves measure compatibility; those are not rows here.
record.test_reason: Not a test. The paper builds a training method (CL2R: fixed d-Simplex classifier plus feature distillation) so that each updated model's features stay directly comparable with its predecessor's. That compatibility is induced on purpose. The models compared are sequential fine-tunes of one lineage, sharing initialization, architecture and the same class-incremental data stream, not independently trained models. The baselines (ER, LwF, BiC and others) measure how much compatibility the methods' own successor checkpoints keep. That bears on catastrophic forgetting, not on whether independent models converge or map onto one another. Convergent learning (Li et al. 2015) is only cited in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that imposing global stationarity (fixed d-Simplex classifier) plus local stationarity (feature distillation on memory samples only) yields lifelong-compatible representations that beat the baselines on their proposed AC, BC and FC metrics.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains sequential task-updated visual models using fixed d-Simplex classifier prototypes and feature distillation, then evaluates retrieval compatibility. It does not use the original sources' methods for measuring convergence across independently trained networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Compatibility varies with training procedure, task count, dataset, and (for IJB-C) false-acceptance-rate setting. The authors also report sensitivity to episodic-memory size and to evaluating feature distillation only on stored memory samples.

fits_no_version.finding: Class-incremental methods without a compatibility mechanism mostly fail the direct compatibility criterion between a model and its own fine-tuned successor. ER, LwF, BiC and FOSTER have cross-test at or below self-test, and AC is often 0-0.14 on CIFAR10 with five or ten tasks. Explicit training (CL2R) raises AC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Successive fine-tuned checkpoints of one network, under class-incremental learning, are not directly interchangeable for retrieval unless compatibility is explicitly trained.

record.peer_reviewed: ACM Trans. Multim. Comput. Commun. Appl.
record.problems: No model-scale or capability sweep, no independent-seed or cross-architecture comparison, and no alternative representation-similarity measures. Reported uncertainty is absent. Some extracted table text is flattened; the paper reports retrieval verification accuracy rather than direct distance-matrix alignment.
record.rows_left_out: Not all baseline entries for the three-, five-, and ten-task CIFAR and ImageNet20 tables, all IJB-C task-count/FAR combinations, or the Table 9 ablation configurations are transcribed. Table 5 and portions of Tables 3 and 8 are flattened in the supplied text, making some assignments uncertain; Figure 3 gives no exact plotted values. These additional results appear in Tables 3, 5, 8, 9 and Figure 3.

untested.parts: No scaling and no independently trained models across architectures, objectives or data.
No vision-language or paired image-caption data.
No same-architecture models trained from different seeds.
No mapping between independently trained models. Compatibility is only between fine-tuned successors, and is trained in by design.
No feature, neuron or circuit analysis.
No comparison of similarity measures or input distributions as tests of convergence.
No analysis of alignment plateaus or of shared data and objectives as its cause.

record.verdict_notes: This is an engineering paper on backward-compatible lifelong representation learning. Compatibility is the training objective, and the compared models are sequential descendants of one another, so the claim's versions about independent models do not apply. Several reader 'partial' states should be 'absent' under the paper's own criterion (cross-test must exceed self-test).

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability scaling, and no comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or datasets.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language models.
No comparison of same-architecture networks trained from different random initializations.
Tests direct cross-task feature compatibility for visual search, not linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired-data mappings.
No interpretable feature, neuron, or circuit recurrence analysis.
Does not compare alternative similarity measures, neighbour settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs as tests of convergence.
Reports incomplete compatibility in some settings, but does not test whether convergence plateaus across independent models or whether shared data/objectives explain alignment.

rows.subject: ER (experience replay)
rows.operation_detail: Cross-test verification using query features from the updated model and gallery features from the previous model.
rows.note: Cross-test is below the self-test.
rows.check: Cross-test between a model and its own fine-tuned successor in a compatibility-training benchmark; not independent models. Cross-test below self-test means the paper's compatibility criterion (ECC) fails, so 'partial' overstates it. The same applies to r2-r8 and r12-r17 where cross < self.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CL2R on the two-task CIFAR10 and ImageNet20 evaluations, and on ImageNet100 with two tasks; LFW with two, three, and five tasks
reader_labels.reason: CL2R cross-test verification exceeds self-test in the two cited two-task tests (r9, r18), and AC is 1.00 in the cited ImageNet100 and LFW settings (r22, r26, r28, r30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Other evaluated procedures and settings, including CL2R with three ImageNet100 tasks and ten LFW tasks
reader_labels.reason: Compatibility is incomplete or lower than the reference self-test in several settings; CL2R AC is 0.67 with three ImageNet100 tasks and 0.82 with ten LFW tasks, while several baselines have lower cross-test scores (r1-r8, r10-r20, r24, r32, r33-r39).
